# Mission: M-war-machine-aif-completion

<!-- engine: structural header, AI-written -->
**Date:** 2026-05-17
**Status:** OPEN — exit criterion #2 satisfied; HEAD-as-escrow scaffold (claude-1, PM pass for the futon-stack-as-Hyperreal-business mission cluster); awaiting Joe verbatims via simulated `eoi-engine` `eoi-inward-mission` flash. **Exit criterion source:** §0 of `~/code/futon7/holes/M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack.md`, criterion #2.
**Bar (lifted verbatim from §0):** *"War Machine ≥ ukrn-services-simulation coherence — concretely: ~12 clojure notebooks (substrate + dynamics + engagement on v2 side; belief + kernel + forward model + EFE + trace on v3 side); test harness with regression baselines; figure-rendering pipeline; R1-R12 (or F1-F10) completeness contract satisfied. Today's War Machine is `:π-display`-only — a reading surface, no belief state, no predictive forward model, no EFE-scored action ranking. The gap is substantial — weeks of work, not hours."*
**Timebox:** estimated 3-4 weeks; final cap is Joe's call at §1.5 verbatim authoring.
**Owner:** Joe (futon7); engineering ownership undefined pending Q-CL1 (see §3.1).
**Sequencing role:** Sibling to `M-stack-essay` and `M-stack-essay-code-alignment` in the mission cluster; predecessor for `M-stack-morphogenetic-rewrite`. **Hard predecessor:** none in the cluster; outside the cluster, depends on `M-interim-director`'s arm-G work (substrate-2 already operational) and on Arms A/B/F producing live data the forward model can train on / score against.
**Cross-ref:**
- `~/code/ukrn-services-simulation/README.md` + `notebooks/ukrn_v3_*.clj` — the predecessor exemplar; the bar this mission graduates the War Machine to
- `~/code/ukrn-services-simulation/docs/aif-completeness.md` — R1-R12 contract; companion to F1-F10 below
- `~/code/futon0/docs/stack-fitness-completeness.md` — F1-F10 stack-fitness contract; the homeostat analogue of R1-R12
- `~/code/futon7/holes/M-interim-director-proxy-metric-inventory.md` §2.5 (math trajectory L1-L5), §2.6 (stack-fitness trajectory L1-L5) — these levels are this mission's *sub-deliverable map*
- `~/code/futon2/scripts/futon2/report/war_machine.clj` — current War Machine surface (2850 lines, single namespace `futon2.report.war-machine`). 13 `scan-*` projection functions; AIF observer at lines 1803–2060 (`observation-channels`, `observe`, `sense->vector`, `preferences`, `avoided-states`, `mode-prior`, `pragmatic-weights`, `compute-free-energy`, `infer-mode`); plus `evaluate-mark2-batches`, `scan-aif-heads`, `load-invariant-inventory`, `enrich-support-attack`, `judge`. **Precision on the §0 Bar quote:** "no belief state" understates current state — there is a mode-prior + mode-inference observer. The accurate baseline is: **`:π-display`-only at the policy/action layer** (no forward model `(state, action) → predicted-state`, no EFE-scored action ranking); a mode-inference observer already exists. The completion gap is forward-model + action-space + EFE-scored policy ranking + test harness + regression fixtures, not "AIF substrate from scratch."
- `~/code/futon3c/src/futon3c/portfolio/observe.clj` — 16-channel portfolio surface
- `~/code/futon3/holes/war-bulletin-9.md` — strategic context (WR-16: operationalised exploit-loops as observation channels)
- `~/code/futon4/README-rewriting.md` — typed-rewrite discipline; the WM's belief updates are operadic-by-construction (Q-SA3)

**Authors:** Joe (verbatim answers, pending); claude-1 (engine-side ordering and minimal structural connective tissue, 2026-05-17 PM scaffold).

fragments.text: # Mission: M-war-machine-aif-completion
fragments.rationale: Names the mission and its id; the rest of the head describes what this mission intends to do to the War Machine.

pattern_rejections.reason: WR-5 says the War Machine is continuously running infrastructure and that new scans, channels or modes are maintenance, not new missions. This document frames the completion work as a mission with a 3-4 week timebox. The head does not mention WR-5, so the two are left side by side here, not reconciled.
pattern_rejections.query: mission header declares status, owner, timebox and exit criterion

fragments.text: <!-- engine: structural header, AI-written -->
fragments.rationale: An HTML comment saying the header was written by a machine engine, not by Joe. So the fields below (status, bar, owner) are scaffold text; only the quoted Bar is stated to come from elsewhere.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern separates agent-view from operator-turn evidence in a mining pipeline's tags. This comment marks authorship of a document header; it is not a tag on an extracted hinge.
pattern_rejections.query: header marks the text as machine-written scaffold, distinct from operator words

fragments.target: the creation date of the scaffold
fragments.rationale: Gives the date the head was written, the same date as the PM scaffold named in the Status and Authors lines.

fragments.text: **Status:** OPEN — exit criterion #2 satisfied
fragments.target: the mission's status and its exit criterion #2
fragments.rationale: The status line calls the mission open and says exit criterion #2 is satisfied. No artifact is named here that shows the criterion met, so as a source for this reading it is a claim by the scaffold, not an outcome.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern tells whoever takes up a mission to re-derive its status from the body and dependencies instead of trusting the banner. It bears on how to read this line, but the fragment itself only states a status, so it is not an instance.
pattern_rejections.query: exit criterion satisfied claim in mission status line

pattern_rejections.reason: WR-25 keeps unanchored good news from moving numerical posteriors until an artifact supports it. Its subject is posterior updates in a buyer-probability model; the criterion claim here has no such model behind it.
pattern_rejections.query: exit criterion satisfied claim in mission status line

fragments.text: HEAD-as-escrow scaffold (claude-1, PM pass for the futon-stack-as-Hyperreal-business mission cluster)
fragments.target: the mission HEAD as a placeholder written by claude-1
fragments.rationale: Says the head is a scaffold held in escrow, written by claude-1 in a PM pass, not a finished statement of Joe's intentions.

pattern_refs.rationale: The document uses the WR-15 name for itself. WR-15 lets a mission HEAD hold intentions in escrow and name every not-yet-committed piece as a tension, instead of pretending a predecessor's schema is settled. Here the pending pieces are Joe's verbatims and the Q-CL1 ownership question; the header does not say the escrow is about a predecessor's data shape, which is what WR-15 describes.

fragments.text: awaiting Joe verbatims via simulated `eoi-engine` `eoi-inward-mission` flash.
fragments.target: Joe's own first-person answers, not yet given
fragments.rationale: The Joe-voiced content is still missing; a simulated flash from the engine stands in for it. Nothing in this head is Joe answering the mission's questions.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern says an answer must be given in the operator's first person, and that an answer in anyone else's voice is a category error. The head keeps Joe's answers marked as pending instead of writing them in the scaffold's voice, which is consistent with that; the pattern is about hinge-pool questions, not mission escrow.

fragments.text: **Exit criterion source:** §0 of `~/code/futon7/holes/M-descriptive-essay-of-the-stack.md`, criterion #2.
fragments.rationale: The exit criterion is defined in another document; this line only says where.

pattern_rejections.reason: It asks for a scope line with in-bounds, out-of-bounds and an exit condition stated up front. Here the exit condition is only cited by location, and no out-of-bounds is given.
pattern_rejections.query: mission header declares status, owner, timebox and exit criterion

fragments.text: **Bar (lifted verbatim from §0):**
fragments.rationale: Says the quoted Bar is copied word for word from §0, so its wording belongs to that source and not to the scaffold.

fragments.text: *"War Machine ≥ ukrn-services-simulation coherence — concretely: ~12 clojure notebooks (substrate + dynamics + engagement on v2 side; belief + kernel + forward model + EFE + trace on v3 side); test harness with regression baselines; figure-rendering pipeline; R1-R12 (or F1-F10) completeness contract satisfied.
fragments.target: what the War Machine has to match: the ukrn-services-simulation exemplar
fragments.rationale: Sets the target by comparison with an existing system: notebooks, a test harness with regression baselines, a figure pipeline, and a completeness contract met.

pattern_refs.rationale: The bar is defined by an external application (ukrn-services-simulation) that this mission takes as its predecessor exemplar; s10 says so directly. WR-11 is the ruling that such a predecessor should be treated as an operational blueprint and its relationship recorded in the spine.

fragments.text: Today's War Machine is `:π-display`-only — a reading surface, no belief state, no predictive forward model, no EFE-scored action ranking.
fragments.target: the War Machine as it stands on 2026-05-17
fragments.rationale: Says the present system only displays: no belief state, no predictive forward model, no EFE-scored ranking of actions. The claim about belief state is corrected in the s14 precision note.

pattern_refs.rationale: Names the same gap: R4 asks for a pure (state, action) to next-state-distribution function that the agent uses to score candidate actions before acting. The fragment says that function does not exist yet.

pattern_rejections.reason: WR-18 (2026-05-31, after this head) says to treat the War Machine as demonstrated infrastructure that drove a full mission lifecycle. It concerns whether the system does real work, not whether it has a forward model, and it postdates the document.
pattern_rejections.query: current state is a reading surface with no forward model, no belief, no action ranking

fragments.text: The gap is substantial — weeks of work, not hours."*
fragments.rationale: An effort estimate of weeks, not hours, given in prose with no breakdown.

fragments.text: estimated 3-4 weeks
fragments.rationale: A calendar range only, with no split between AI and human effort and no confidence level.

pattern_rejections.reason: It prescribes an estimate with tokens, hours per person, and a confidence level. The header gives only a range of weeks, so it does not follow that schema.
pattern_rejections.query: estimate effort in weeks with the final cap left to the operator

fragments.text: final cap is Joe's call at §1.5 verbatim authoring
fragments.rationale: The hard limit is not set here; it is left for Joe to decide when he writes his verbatims at §1.5.

fragments.text: **Owner:** Joe (futon7)
fragments.rationale: Names Joe, under futon7, as owner of the mission.

fragments.text: engineering ownership undefined pending Q-CL1 (see §3.1)
fragments.rationale: Says engineering ownership is not yet decided and points to question Q-CL1 in §3.1 as what would settle it.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern says an open question belongs in a document only if bound to a named way of closing it. Here the question is named (Q-CL1, §3.1); whether §3.1 names a role, event or evidence that closes it is not visible in this head.

fragments.text: **Sequencing role:** Sibling to `M-stack-essay` and `M-stack-essay-code-alignment` in the mission cluster; predecessor for `M-stack-morphogenetic-rewrite`.
fragments.target: this mission's place among its siblings and successor
fragments.rationale: Says where the mission sits: beside two cluster siblings, and before M-stack-morphogenetic-rewrite.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern asks for missions to be linked by explicit typed relationships (blocks, enables, shares, parent-child) so dependencies are visible. This line gives sibling and predecessor relations in prose.

fragments.text: **Hard predecessor:** none in the cluster; outside the cluster, depends on `M-interim-director`'s arm-G work (substrate-2 already operational)
fragments.target: what must exist before this mission can proceed
fragments.rationale: Says nothing inside the cluster blocks this mission, and that outside it the mission depends on M-interim-director's arm-G work. The parenthesis 'substrate-2 already operational' is the scaffold's own claim.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern says a blocked mission must cite its specific blocker. This line names the blocker (arm-G work of M-interim-director) and says there is none inside the cluster.

fragments.text: and on Arms A/B/F producing live data the forward model can train on / score against.
fragments.target: live data from Arms A, B and F
fragments.rationale: The forward model, which does not exist yet, needs live data from three arms for training or scoring, so its completion depends on those arms.

pattern_refs.rationale: A shared-resource dependency: the mission cannot finish a step until other missions' arms produce data, which the pattern's 'shares' and 'blocked-by' relations are for.

fragments.rationale: Corrects the quoted Bar against the code: there is a mode prior and a mode-inference observer, so 'no belief state' is too strong.

pattern_refs.rationale: This is the pattern's disagreement case: the requirement text (the §0 Bar) says one thing and the implementation says another, and the disagreement is written down.

pattern_refs.rationale: The pattern says that when most of the required function already exists in a tested script, add to it instead of writing a replacement. Here the mode-inference observer is kept and only the missing parts are named; the doc does not say the existing code is tested or that 80% exists.
R6 states the problem of a candidate action space and selection. 'Action-space' is one of the listed gaps, so this problem node is where that item lands.
